data.why: The app stores records only in session state and has no bundled example data, so a small CSV matching its experiment-record schema (including a missing-value row and a mass-loss outlier) lets a scientist test CSV import/export.

goals: Calculate specimen mass loss and weight-loss corrosion rate (mm/year) from initial/final mass, density, area, and exposure time
Estimate electrochemical corrosion rate from corrosion current density, equivalent weight, and density
Compare a blank and an inhibited corrosion rate to compute inhibition efficiency (%)
Build up an experiment log of saved calculation results and manual records, then export it as CSV
Import a CSV of prior experiment records to review or append to the current session's log
Save and search literature notes by keyword alongside the experiment records

review.summary: The tree captures CorroScope's purpose and workflow faithfully: weight-loss and electrochemical rate calculators, inhibition efficiency, a session experiment log with CSV import/export, and literature notes. Labels, depth, features and most cited screens are sound. It should not be filed as is, because its main 'import is broken' finding comes from the run's own malformed sample CSV (unquoted commas) and is misdiagnosed. The import/export evidence needs to be redone with a valid file and the explanation corrected.
